source: GIZ (Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit), Support of Regional Economic Cooperation in Asia (SRECA), in cooperation with MAFF General Directorate of Agriculture — គោលការណ៍ណែនាំអំពីការនាំចេញផ្លែស្វាយស្រស់ពីប្រទេសកម្ពុជាទៅប្រទេសចិន (Guideline on Fresh Mango Export from Cambodia to China), Final Version, Phnom Penh, December 2020, 67pp
text:
Procedure for preparing harvested mango and obtaining the phytosanitary certificate needed for export to China, per the GIZ/SRECA guideline (December 2020 edition). This covers the later farm-level steps in the guideline's overall registration/export flow.

Harvest and de-sapping: fruit for export should be harvested at the correct physiological maturity (rather than left to over-ripen on the tree) and handled carefully to avoid dropping or bruising. The stem is cut and the fruit is de-sapped (allowed to drain its latex/sap) properly, since sap that runs onto the skin can cause sapburn blemishes that downgrade the fruit.

Vapor Heat Treatment (VHT): fruit intended for the China market undergoes a quarantine disinfestation treatment using controlled hot water vapor applied to bring the fruit's internal temperature to a specified level for a set holding time, in order to kill any fruit fly eggs or larvae before export. The guideline gives specific temperature and duration figures for this process, but the exact numbers were difficult to confirm with full confidence from the scanned source at the resolution available and should be verified against the original document (or current GACC protocol) before being used as a compliance reference.

Certificate request procedure: once fruit has been harvested, treated, and packed, the exporter submits a request for phytosanitary inspection and certificate issuance to the plant quarantine authority. The inspector verifies the shipment against the registered orchard and packing house records (variety, origin orchard, volume, treatment record) before issuing the phytosanitary certificate that accompanies the shipment to the Cambodia-China border.

Rejected or non-compliant fruit: the guideline notes that fruit which fails inspection (for pest presence, documentation mismatch, or quality defects) should be identified and separated before it reaches the certification stage, since mixing non-compliant fruit into a certified shipment risks the whole consignment being rejected at the Chinese border.
caveat: This document is very likely the same GIZ/SRECA fresh-mango-export-to-China guideline series already represented as mango Source C in the knowledge base (processed in Batch 43), but this is a later, more complete edition (dated December 2020, 67pp, vs. the earlier-processed 53pp version with data through 2018). Some content below (market/policy context, registration procedures, marketing section) is likely NEW relative to Source C; other content (GACC protocol, phytosanitary basics, documentation) likely OVERLAPS with Source C. This has not been reconciled against Source C's actual files — a duplicate-check comparing this source (tagged G) against Source C is recommended before both are considered final. Contains specific VHT technical detail that is likely genuinely useful and may be new relative to Source C; flagged with a caveat on unverified numeric details.
